entries.title: Why this, and not HTML→PDF?
entries.text: Most "HTML to PDF" tools drive a headless browser and screenshot the page — the result is an image, text is not selectable, and pagination is an afterthought. pdf-report-engine lays out, line-breaks, paginates and embeds glyphs in-process , emitting true vector text. It is built…

entries.title: Features
entries.text: Authoring & pagination Describe a report as data or simple markup and the engine lays it out, breaks lines and paginates it — with repeating headers, group totals and page numbers, just like a classic reporting tool. Styling & layout A familiar CSS look: real selectors and a mode…

entries.title: Build a report in the online editor
entries.text: Try the engine without setting up a project. Author a report in HTML with the block palette and properties panel, edit data, then generate and preview the PDF right in your browser. Visual authoring Insert report blocks, adjust their properties, and work directly with the support…

entries.title: How it works
entries.text: Two entry points funnel through one pipeline: renderToBuffer(report, options?) — one-shot: IR in, PDF bytes out. renderToStream(report, options?) — returns a ReadableStream for incremental delivery. createReport(report, options?) — the live pdfkit doc plus the paginated pages mod…

entries.text: Continue to Getting started for fonts, data-driven tables and the CLI.

entries.title: Requirements
entries.text: Node.js ≥ 18 — the package is ESM-only ( "type": "module" ). Runtime dependencies: pdfkit and fontkit . Everything else is a dev dependency.

entries.title: Your first report (IR)
entries.text: The report is a plain data object — ReportDoc . It is serialisable, diffable and validatable without any parser. Without embedding fonts, the standard PDF base-14 fonts (like Helvetica ) render out of the box, so a first report needs nothing installed.

entries.title: Embedding fonts
entries.text: To use real font programs (and non-Latin scripts), register them with readFontFiles . It reads from disk paths or from bytes you already have. Prefer a graceful fallback: filter candidates with fs.existsSync() and pass fonts: [] when none are found — the base-14 fonts still rende…

entries.title: Running in the browser
entries.text: The core engine is pure JavaScript and bundles for the browser — the library graph has no top-level node:* imports . Two constraints remain: pdfkit itself needs Buffer /streams, so build with a Node-polyfill plugin (Vite: vite-plugin-node-polyfills ; webpack: resolve.fallback );…

entries.title: Web fonts & Google Fonts
entries.text: You don't have to fetch bytes by hand. When the HTML references a web font, the engine resolves and embeds it during renderToBuffer — the same code runs in Node and in the browser . htmlToReportDoc collects Google Fonts <link> / @import and inline @font-face rules into report.fon…

entries.title: Data-driven tables
entries.text: Feed an array into dataSource ; the detail template expands once per row, groups produce breaks and subtotal footers, and column headers repeat on every page the table spans (set repeatHeader: false to opt out). Cells are not limited to text. Add blocks to a cell to stack any flo…

entries.title: Breaks & keep-together
entries.text: Pagination fills a vertical cursor down the page, one fragment at a time. A paragraph becomes one fragment per typeset line — that is why prose flows freely across pages. Table rows normally move as a unit when they do not fit in the remaining space. If a top-aligned, text-only d…

entries.title: Charts
entries.text: A chart block draws bar , line , area , pie , donut , combo , waterfall , scatter , bubble , radar , gauge and heatmap charts with the same primitives as the rest of the engine: real vector marks and selectable labels, no canvas and no charting library. A chart is laid out as one…

entries.text: Every heading emits an outline entry — the bookmark tree PDF readers show in their sidebar. Entries nest by heading level automatically, and a heading on a later page still attaches under the chapter opened earlier. Any block with an id also becomes a named destination. A toc blo…

entries.text: Text wrapped in <a href> becomes a clickable link in the generated PDF. External URLs ( https://… ) open in the reader’s browser; internal anchors ( #section-name ) jump to the matching id within the document. Links are underlined and coloured automatically (via the style cascade…

entries.title: Author with HTML
entries.text: Prefer markup? The adapter parses a forgiving HTML/CSS subset into the same IR. The HTML subset understands colspan / rowspan , per-cell colours and borders, data-band for page headers/footers, and running {PAGE} tokens. A block-level becomes an embedded image. You can set…

entries.text: A background box can be rounded , shadowed and filled with a linear gradient — authored straight from the HTML subset ( border-radius , box-shadow , background: linear-gradient(…) ) or set on the IR as borderRadius / boxShadow / backgroundImage . Everything stays vector: the roun…

entries.title: Capture a live browser element
entries.text: In a browser, htmlElementToReportDoc reads the selected element's current content and computed styles, including external CSS and styles applied by page JavaScript. Call it after the page has reached the state to capture. It maps those styles into the engine's supported report la…

entries.title: Images (offline & online)
entries.text: An ImageBlock takes a local path, a data: URI, raw bytes, or an http(s) URL. Offline sources render synchronously; remote URLs are fetched by renderToBuffer 's pre-pass.

entries.title: SVG vector images
entries.text: An svg block draws an SVG document as real PDF paths — no rasterisation, no canvas, no resolution ceiling. Inline <svg> markup, data:image/svg+xml URIs, .svg file paths, raw bytes and remote http(s) URLs all take the same code path; the image pre-pass fetches remote sources befor…

entries.title: Flexbox layout
entries.text: A display: flex container lays out any flow blocks along a row or a column. The engine implements a pragmatic CSS-flexbox subset: main-axis direction, optional wrap, justify-content , align-items / align-self , gap and per-item flex-grow / flex-shrink / flex-basis . A flex contai…

entries.title: CSS Grid layout
entries.text: The HTML adapter supports a report-focused subset of display: grid : explicit fixed, percentage, or fr columns, repeat() , gaps, row-major auto-placement, and grid-row / grid-column: span N . Rows grow to fit their content. This is a PDF layout mapping, not browser rendering; int…

entries.title: Rich inline text
entries.text: Per-run style overrides within a paragraph are fully supported: bold , italic , underline , strikethrough , colour, font-size, background highlight, and opacity — all via inline HTML elements or style attributes. Each styled span becomes an InlineSource with a sparse StyleProps o…

entries.title: Page watermark
entries.text: A declarative watermark is rendered diagonally across every page as filled vector glyph outlines (not PDF text operators), so it cannot be selected or extracted by text search. Add it via <meta name="watermark"> in HTML, or the watermark field on the ReportDoc IR. By default it s…

entries.title: Multi-column layout
entries.text: Distribute child blocks across N equal-width columns using CSS column-count or the data-columns attribute. The engine sequentially fills columns by height (total / count). The ColumnBlock is kept atomic (never splits across pages). Vertical rules are optional lines drawn at colum…

entries.text: Pin a block at exact page coordinates, stack it above or below the body with z-index , and turn it with rotate (CSS transform: rotate() or the data-rotate attribute) — all outside the normal flow. Any top-level block (or a block inside a band) can leave the vertical flow and be p…

entries.title: Streaming output
entries.text: renderToStream() returns a ReadableStream<Uint8Array> that flushes each page incrementally, reducing peak memory for server-side rendering. Internally this sets bufferPages: false , which tells pdfkit to flush each page’s encoded stream as soon as the next page starts — the ideal…

entries.text: Set encrypt on the ReportDoc to write a password-protected PDF through pdfkit's standard security handler (RC4 128-bit). A userPassword gates opening the file; an ownerPassword gates changing permissions (one is generated if you omit it). At least one password must be present — o…

entries.title: Password-protect a report
entries.text: Add encrypt to any ReportDoc to write a protected PDF. The output is unencrypted (unchanged bytes) unless you set at least one password.

entries.title: Streaming with createReport
entries.text: The lower-level, synchronous entry returns the pdfkit doc and the paginated pages array, so you can pipe the bytes to any writable stream.

entries.title: Page bands & running tokens (IR)
entries.text: Bands repeat on every page; {PAGE} / {TOTAL} (or $page.number / $page.total in expressions) resolve per page only inside bands.

entries.text: Task bars render at proportional positions, progress fills darker sub-bars, and dependencies draw L-shaped arrows. See samples/gantt.html .

entries.title: Streaming PDF output
entries.text: renderToStream() forces bufferPages: false internally, so each page’s bytes flush as soon as the next starts — lower peak memory for large documents.

entries.text: These options are passed as RenderOptions.images or as the second argument to resolveRemoteImages(report, options) . A custom resolveImage(url) returns image bytes, or null when it cannot resolve that URL; onError controls whether a failure throws or skips that asset.
